title: Eye Contact
description: How people use their gaze to communicate interest, dominance, confidence, or anxiety.

sections.title: Quick Understanding
sections.content: Eye contact is one of the most powerful forms of nonverbal communication. Where people look, how long they look, and when they look away provides a real-time map of their confidence, comfort level, and what they are paying attention to.

sections.title: What It Looks Like
content: Maintaining a steady, relaxed gaze.
Looking away repeatedly during a conversation.
Staring intensely without blinking.
Rapidly darting eyes around the room or checking the door.

sections.title: What It May Indicate
content: High interest or attraction (prolonged gaze, dilated pupils).
Dominance or aggression (unblinking, hard staring).
Anxiety or discomfort (rapid blinking, avoiding gaze).
Deep thought (looking up or away while processing a complex question).

sections.title: What It Does NOT Mean
content: Looking away does NOT automatically mean someone is lying.
Staring directly does NOT automatically mean someone is telling the truth.
Avoiding eye contact does NOT always mean someone is insecure (it may be a cultural sign of respect, or they are just thinking).

sections.title: Real Life Examples
content: Date: Prolonged, soft eye contact holding slightly longer than socially standard.
Workplace: A boss holding unbroken eye contact to assert authority during a tough negotiation.
Argument: Someone refusing to make eye contact strictly when confronted with a difficult truth.
Sales: A customer rapidly darting their eyes toward the exit, signaling they want to leave.

sections.title: Cluster Analysis
content: Intense eye contact + relaxed posture + smiling = High interest / Attraction.
Intense eye contact + tight jaw + rigid posture = Aggression / Intimidation.
Avoiding eye contact + fidgeting + crossed arms = Discomfort / Anxiety.

sections.title: Common Situations
content: Job interviews (evaluating confidence).
Romantic dates (evaluating mutual interest).
Interrogations or confrontations (power dynamics).
Sales pitches (building trust).

sections.title: Observation Mistakes
sections.content: Mistake: Assuming strong eye contact equals honesty. Reality: Confident, practiced liars often deliberately maintain intense, unbroken eye contact specifically to 'prove' they are telling the truth.

sections.title: Practical Observation Tips
content: Notice when the eye contact breaks. Does it break exactly on a specific difficult question?
Watch for the 'hard stare' vs the 'soft gaze'. A hard stare feels piercing; a soft gaze feels inviting.
Look at the blink rate. A sudden, massive increase in blinking often indicates a severe spike in stress.

sections.title: Red Flags
content: An unnatural, unblinking stare that feels highly predatory or completely emotionless.
Someone who normally has great eye contact suddenly refusing to look at you when a specific topic is brought up.
Someone aggressively overcompensating with intense eye contact when making a highly dubious claim.

sections.title: Reality Check
sections.content: Eye contact is heavily influenced by culture, neurodivergence (like ADHD or Autism), and social anxiety. Never use eye contact alone to broadly judge someone's character or honesty. It must always be measured strictly against their personal, normal baseline behavior.
